turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: Hi Dana, Sara at HyperSale. We help RevOps teams shorten new-hire ramp through AI buyer practice; how are reps practicing before live calls today?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: We already have Gong for this—call libraries, coaching, all of it. What’s different about what you’re offering?

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: Gong coaches after real calls; HyperSale lets reps rehearse before them, with every score tied to an exact quote. Do new hires rehearse?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: That’s a fair distinction—new hires mostly practice on live prospects today. But my managers don’t have time for another tool.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: That’s why practice is self-guided; managers review weekly improvement rather than run roleplays. If it took 15 minutes weekly, would that feel manageable?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Maybe, but my managers barely listen to Gong recordings now. How would I measure whether the practice is actually improving ramp or attach rate?

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: We’d baseline time-to-first-qualified-meeting and attach rate, then compare pilot reps over 30 days. What ramp metric do you trust most today?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Time to first qualified opportunity is the cleanest ramp metric for us. But we just renewed Gong, and there’s no budget this year.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: Understood—this wouldn’t replace Gong. Could we scope a 30-day pilot for one new-hire cohort, using time-to-first-qualified-opportunity to build next year’s budget case?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: If the 30-day pilot is under $15,000, I can sponsor it. Send me a one-page scope and two times for a 20-minute working session next week; I've got a meeting, I need to go.
